decision: Accept the two complete independently reviewed official whole-imada footprints under the existing source-preserving conflict policy. This replaces the proven false New Chenini GPS label at the western village, while retaining explicit ambiguity in conflicting areas. This is a bounded data improvement, not a seamless regional partition or complete catalog certification.
reviewOfPreviousHold: The source-readiness hold required root review of the substantial mixed-source overlap and coverage delta. That review is now complete. Existing accepted-boundary policy and actual runtime do not require replacing every obsolete neighbor first. The previous hold is resolved for these two identities only; all neighboring candidates remain separate.

sourceAcceptance.identityCrosscheck: Current INS registry based on original 2024 census workbooks; dated 2023 decree establishes one whole-imada electoral circle per identity. Separate old/new village identity evidence includes the IRA/IRD field study and public landmarks.

legacyCoverageDelta.meaning: Changes relative to older sector claims, including open areas; not certified land coverage.

coverageAcceptance.reason: Preserve and mark every positive-area source disagreement using the existing conflict detector. Do not prefer one conflicting claim or invent a border. Reduced specificity is accepted in these disputed intersections and uncovered source gaps because no supported precise identity is available there.
coverageAcceptance.actualCoordinateReview: All3632 raw catalog coordinates and259 original prayer-source anchors were examined. Only the two villages and the two artificial sector references lie in old/proposed Chenini2 coverage; western village resolves correctly, eastern remains correct, and no current named source point loses a polygon label. The old New Chenini sector representative is corrected through its separately reviewed eastern village manual anchor.
coverageAcceptance.gapEvidence: 33 unique enclosed components total about29.11km2. No current catalog point or nonsector locality footprint intersects them. This does not establish absence of inhabitants, unnamed places, or omitted settlements. The29 components above1m2 return no precise locality at their examined interior points. Four numerically degenerate tiny components retain explicitly reported edge/projection effects.
